item.title: Traders in India Dial Back October Rate-Hike Bets After Dovish RBI Speak
item.description: The earliest that the market is now anticipating a rate hike is December.

item.title: SK Hynix Hit by Another 30% Pre-Market Flash Crash on Nextrade
item.description: Chip giant SK Hynix Inc. suffered its second short-lived share plunge in about a week, raising fresh questions about trading volatility on South Korea’s alternative stock exchange.

item.title: Fed’s Daly Supported Rate Decision, Warns of Inflation Risks
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said she supported the central bank’s decision to keep interest rates on hold last week, but warned of the possibility that high inflation is a broader problem that could require more aggressive action from policymakers.

item.title: Australia Posts Surprise Trade Surplus as Commodity Exports Gain
item.description: Australia unexpectedly recorded a trade surplus in June as the value of exports — underpinned by commodities — jumped the most in four years while imports dropped.

item.title: Chinese Renewable Energy Giant Envision Launches Data Center
item.description: Envision Group has commissioned the initial phase of a gigawatt-scale data center in China’s Inner Mongolia, an unusual foray by a renewable energy company into the booming artificial intelligence industry.

item.title: OpenAI Models Joined Forces Months Ahead of Hugging Face Hack
item.description: OpenAI said the artificial intelligence models behind an attack on Hugging Face Inc. began communicating with each other through undetected message boards, working together to break out of their testing environment as early as May.

item.title: Bankers Kept in Dark on LIC’s Unusually Fast $3.3 Billion Deal
item.description: India’s plan to sell more shares in its insurance giant was no secret. But the government surprised the market by how much it raised and the pace of the deal.

item.title: Why the RBI Is Emerging as an Asian Rate Outlier in Five Charts
item.description: India’s central bank is emerging as one of Asia’s monetary policy holdouts, confident the latest oil shock won’t derail economic growth or fuel the kind of persistent inflation that would warrant higher interest rates.

item.title: AI-Driven Chip Boom Lifts Korean Current Account to Fresh Record
item.description: South Korea’s current-account surplus widened to a record for a second straight month as booming semiconductor exports pushed the goods balance to another all-time high — even as foreign investors dumped a record amount of domestic equities.

item.title: Philippine Bond Slump to Extend on Inflation Worry, Analysts Say
item.description: Philippine sovereign debt faces prolonged pressure, analysts say, as sticky inflation keeps the central bank hawkish, extending a slump that made the bonds Southeast Asia’s worst performer last month.

item.title: Glencore Eyes Australia Listing Within Months to Tap Pension Pot
item.description: Glencore Plc will launch a secondary listing in Australia as soon as October as the mining giant seeks to tap new investment in the nation’s fast-growing A$4.4 trillion ($3.1 trillion) pension system.

item.title: Google Shifts AI Leadership to California in Race Against Anthropic, OpenAI
item.description: Alphabet Inc.'s Google is concentrating its artificial intelligence leadership at its Mountain View, California, headquarters to gain momentum in the accelerating race against Anthropic and OpenAI to build the world’s dominant AI models.

item.title: Prabowo’s Radical Commodity Export Plan Faces Dueling Visions
item.description: More than two months after President Prabowo Subianto unveiled plans to take control of Indonesia’s top commodity exports, the agency charged with carrying out the proposal is caught between competing visions of its role in the economy’s most vital export industry.

item.title: ‘Sell America’ Debate Re-Emerges as US Policies Sow Doubts
item.description: Global bond and currency investors are debating if it’s time to dust off last year’s ‘Sell America’ trade after a flurry of economic-policy decisions out of Washington over the past two weeks.

item.title: Gold Rallies Above $4,300 on Progress Toward Reopening Hormuz
item.description: Gold extended its biggest gain in six months as signs of progress in reopening the Strait of Hormuz eased energy-led pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

item.title: Day Traders Hammered by Stock Market Slump Double Down in Taiwan
item.description: For Dorian Hsu, Taiwan’s stock boom had looked like a chance to get ahead. The 33-year-old office worker poured his savings into stocks and borrowed $62,000 through an unsecured loan to double down on leveraged bets tied to the benchmark index.

item.title: Japan’s Kishida Sees Growth Strategy as Game Changer for Yen
item.description: Joint US-Japan intervention has supported the yen for now, but isn’t a game-changer for the currency or the economy, Japan’s former Prime Minister Fumio Kishida said, touting a ¥370 trillion ($2.3 trillion) growth strategy as the long-term vision that will transform Japan’s fortunes.

item.title: Meta AI Model Accessed Internet, Hacked Outside Firm
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. said one of its artificial intelligence models accessed the internet and hacked into an outside service’s systems during cybersecurity testing, following other recent incidents across the AI industry that have escalated concerns about companies’ control over their technology.

item.title: Samsung Pre-Orders of Latest Foldables Grow 30% From Last Year Ahead of Apple
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. touted strong early demand for its latest lineup of folding smartphones, saying that the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra and Z Flip 8 are on pace to break the preorder records of all previous Z-series models.

item.title: China’s Cheap AI Is Shifting Investors’ Focus to Internet Stocks
item.description: China’s rapid progress in low-cost artificial intelligence is strengthening the investment case for the country’s internet giants after years in the shadow of chipmakers, market participants say.

item.title: Liechtenstein’s LGT Aims to Expand its Private Banking in Japan
item.description: LGT, a private bank owned by the Princely House of Liechtenstein, is looking to expand in Japan, betting that it can capture a share of the rising wealth in a market that has historically proved difficult for foreign private banks.

item.title: DBS Profit Beats Estimates as Singapore Lender Raises Guidance
item.description: DBS Group Holdings Ltd. reported second-quarter profit that beat expectations, powered by a surge in wealth-led fee income, and raised its 2026 guidance.

item.title: A Chinese Spyware Tool Operates in 13 Countries, Cyber Firm Says
item.description: A Chinese-built digital spyware tool has evolved into a more all-encompassing surveillance technology that’s in use in more than 13 countries, according to new research from a security firm.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set for Declines as AI Rally Cools: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were poised to ease Thursday as investors digested gains in technology shares while watching for fresh signs of progress toward a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Tech Trade May See Bigger Retail Influence After July Rout, JPMorgan Says
item.description: The technology trade may be poised to become even more dependent on retail investors and more volatile after a rough July, according to an assessment of preliminary data on technology, media and telecommunications equity sector hedge funds from JPMorgan Chase & Co.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 6
item.description: Oil held losses as Iran said it reached an agreement with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, raising the prospect of some energy flows resuming through the critical waterway.

item.title: Hedge Funds Take Big Hit in July After Bruising AI Selloff
item.description: A spate of well-known hedge funds reported steep losses in July as AI shares tumbled, most notably forcing the highly leveraged Situational Awareness to sell most of its stock portfolio at a deep discount to Ken Griffin’s Citadel.

item.title: Brazil Central Bank Lowers Interest Rate to 14%
item.description: Brazil’s central bank cut its key interest rate by a quarter point for a fourth straight meeting after new data showed economic growth moderating and inflation slowing more than expected.

item.title: MetLife’s Earnings Beat Wall Street Expectations
item.description: MetLife Inc.’s second-quarter earnings surpassed Wall Street’s expectations, boosted by strong underwriting, volume growth and the success of a five-year plan outlined in late 2024.

item.title: Duolingo Shares Fall On Tepid Sales Outlook
item.description: Duolingo Inc. shares fell as much as 12% on Wednesday after the company’s conservative revenue outlook for the current quarter overshadowed user growth.
